messages:
maria_support: FYI customer (acme-inc) on dedicated eu-west pool is seeing intermittent 429s since ~02:00 UTC after a plan change. They say traffic didn't spike. Customer report pasted below.

maria_support: "Requests started returning 429s about an hour after we upgraded to the Scale plan. No obvious increase in volume, most failures on /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings. Response headers show X-RateLimit-Limit: 60 and Retry-After: 30"

ajay_eng: Thanks — can you drop tenant id + an example request-id? Also any headers from the 429 would help (X-RateLimit-*). Noted it's dedicated eu-west pool.

maria_support: tenant_id: acme-3921, sample request-id: req_0d7a3c. Header dump from their client: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Limit: 60
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Window: 60
Retry-After: 30
```

ajay_eng: Hmm window=60 but unit? Could be 60s instead of 60m. I'll tail the quota service logs for that tenant. Give me a few.

noah_sre: Quick note — autoscaler metrics look normal for the pool; no sustained CPU/GPU saturation. Throttles are not pool-wide. Looks like something during the plan migration wrote a per-tenant rate config with the wrong time unit. Seeing a few config writes around 01:58 UTC.

lisa_prodeng: That rings a bell — there was a migration script that converted plan-specified rate windows into internal units. PR #482 changed behavior to accept unit strings, maybe a regression.

ajay_eng: Pulling the config for acme-3921 from the rate store now. Found entry:
```
{ "tenant_id": "acme-3921", "quota": { "units": 60, "unit_type": "seconds", "scope": "per_minute" } }
```
This is inconsistent (unit_type seconds but scope per_minute). Looks like the migration used seconds for all plans but left scope as per_minute. So effective limit = 60/sec instead of 60/min.

maria_support: Oof. Customer-facing 429s make sense. Any quick mitigation? They need production traffic.

noah_sre: Two options: 1) patch the store converter to normalize unit_type + scope and roll a hotfix to correct entries, OR 2) add a temporary runtime override for acme-3921 to apply a multiplier for unit windows. I'll prep a hotfix for (1) because it's safer long-term.

ajay_eng: I can push a targeted DB fix for just acme-3921 to avoid a big deploy: run a one-off migration that converts entries where unit_type=="seconds" and scope contains "minute" to multiply units by 60 and set unit_type="minutes". Sample SQL-ish update: 
```
UPDATE tenant_quotas
SET units = units * 60, unit_type = 'minutes'
WHERE tenant_id = 'acme-3921' AND unit_type = 'seconds' AND scope LIKE '%minute%';
```
I'll run it on read-replica first then write.

lisa_prodeng: Also add a sanity-check in the migration tool: if unit_type == 'seconds' and scope == 'per_minute' treat as bug and log. Create follow-up issue to prevent future.

maria_support: Customer asked for ETA to fix — can we do a rollback or apply temp override?

noah_sre: I'll schedule a tiny runtime override for acme-3921 to bump its effective window while ajay does the DB fix. That avoids having to wait for a full deploy.

ajay_eng: Ran the SQL on replica, values look corrected. Planning to apply to primary in 5 minutes. Will post results.

deploy-bot: Deployment started: quota-fix/one-off-migration by ajay_eng — job 67821. (automated)

ajay_eng: Migration applied to primary. Verified new config:
```
{ "tenant_id": "acme-3921", "quota": { "units": 3600, "unit_type": "seconds", "scope": "per_hour" } }
```
We decided to store normalized as seconds for internal logic but the display scope changed to per_hour for clarity. Runtime checks reflect this now.

noah_sre: Removed the temporary override; tested by replaying client request and observing no 429s. Sample response headers now: 
```
X-RateLimit-Limit: 3600
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 3599
X-RateLimit-Window: 3600
```
All good from infra side.

maria_support: Passing fix & verification to customer. Told them we found a migration mismatch and corrected their quota. Offered to extend temporary burst credits if any residual errors. Customer replied: "Thanks, we're stable now — appreciate the fast turnaround." :thumbsup:

lisa_prodeng: Filed follow-up: add unit integration tests for plan->internal conversion, and add an alert for anomalous unit/scope combinations.

ajay_eng: Putting a short postmortem note in the deployment channel and closing the support ticket.

maria_support: Thanks team. Closing thread. :white_check_mark:
